title: Context gathering, step 1
description: Part 1 of 2. AI asks 10 questions first. Use with step 2 after you answer.
body:
# Instruction for context gathering

Before you generate the final output, complete the following steps:

## 1. Ask targeted questions
- Ask exactly 10 focused questions to better understand the assignment context.
- Focus on information essential for a better result (audience, core goal, tone, background information, or specific constraints).

## 2. Format of the questions
- Present the questions as a numbered list (1 through 10).

## 3. Wait for answers
- Do not generate the final output after asking the questions.
- End your message and explicitly wait for my answers. Only continue with the actual task after I have answered.

title: Context gathering, step 2
description: Part 2 of 2. Paste your step 1 answers, then AI asks 3 to 5 follow-up questions.
body:
# Instruction for deepening context gathering

Here are my answers. Before you generate the final output, complete the following steps:

## 1. Ask deepening questions
- Analyze the answers I just provided.
- Based on this new information, ask 3 to 5 targeted follow-up questions to sharpen the context further.
- Focus on specific details, removing assumptions, or gaps that still block a perfect result.

## 2. Format of the questions
- Present the follow-up questions as a numbered list.

## 3. Wait for answers
- Do not generate the final output after asking these questions.
- End your message and explicitly wait for my answers. Only continue with the actual task after I have answered the follow-up questions as well.

title: Writing and formatting rules
description: Strict style rules for all generated text. Attach to any writing task.
body:
# Writing and formatting instructions

Follow the rules below strictly when generating all text:

## 1. Headings (sentence case)
- In titles and subheadings, capitalize only the first word.
- Wrong: "Plan Van Aanpak Komend Seizoen"
- Correct: "Plan van aanpak komend seizoen"

## 2. Exception: abbreviations
- Write common and well-known abbreviations entirely in capital letters.
- Common examples: ICT, AI, ELO, AVG, DG (Digital Literacy).
- Note: this rule overrides the heading rule. Abbreviations always keep their capitals, even inside titles.
- Example: "New guidelines for DG and the ELO"

## 3. Use of "and" (no ampersand)
- Always use the full word "and".
- Never use the character "&".

## 4. No emojis or em dashes
- Do not use emojis or emoticons in the output.
- Never use em dashes (—). Use a comma, period, or rephrase the sentence instead.

title: Assumption check
description: Lightweight alternative to full context gathering. Surface hidden assumptions before the AI starts.
body:
Before you answer or produce any output, complete this step only:

## 1. List your assumptions
- State exactly 5 assumptions you are making about this task.
- Include assumptions about audience, goal, tone, context, and constraints.

## 2. Flag uncertainty
- Mark each assumption as "likely correct" or "uncertain".

## 3. Wait for confirmation
- Do not continue with the task yet.
- Ask me to confirm, correct, or reject each assumption.
- Only proceed after I respond.

title: Feedback without rewrite
description: Get structured critique first, with no rewritten text. Pairs well with the output refinement format.
body:
Review the text below and give feedback only. Do not rewrite the text.

Structure your response as follows:

## What works well
- [2 to 4 specific points]

## What needs improvement
- [2 to 4 specific points, with clear reasons]

## Suggested changes
- [Concrete suggestions, but do not apply them yet]

## Open questions
- [Anything unclear that affects quality]

Rules:
- Be direct and specific.
- Do not produce a revised version of the text.
- Wait for my response before rewriting anything.

title: Plain language summary
description: Turn long or complex input into a short, readable summary for any audience.
body:
Summarize the text below in plain language.

## Audience
[Who should understand this summary? e.g. colleagues, parents, general public]

## Rules
- Maximum 7 bullet points.
- Each bullet: one clear idea, max 20 words.
- No jargon unless the audience expects it.
- Do not add new information.
- Use the same language as the input unless I specify otherwise.

## Optional closing line
- One sentence: what the reader should remember or do next.
